summary.text: Anna Paulina Luna is the Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 13th Congressional District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.
An Air Force veteran, she worked in conservative advocacy and media, ran unsuccessfully for Congress in 2020, won the seat in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Luna was born in Orange, California, in 1989; according to her congressional office, she was raised by a single mother in Southern California.
She served in the U.S. Air Force from 2009 to 2018 and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of West Florida in 2017. Her congressional biography says the degree is in biology.

She worked as an entrepreneur, as director of Hispanic engagement for Turning Point USA, as chairwoman of Hispanic initiative for PragerU, and as a podcast host with Gingrich 360, and she is a published author with Posthill Press.
Luna ran for Congress in Florida's 13th District in 2020 as the Republican nominee and lost the general election to incumbent Charlie Crist.

She won the 2022 general election for the district, defeating Eric Lynn and other candidates, and took office in January 2023; her office says she is the first Mexican-American woman elected to Congress from Florida.
She serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and she chairs the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets.
Her congressional biography says Time named her one of its next 100 most influential people in 2023 and that she lives in St. Petersburg with her husband, Andy.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 49.5% of the vote to Leela Gray's 48.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
